title: Construct the normalized native common-field functor
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $X$ a Noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension, with $\ell$ a unit in every local ring. There exists a normalized native functor of [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-normalized-functor]. In particular, construct the coefficient presentations, exact section transport, additive triangulated functor, integral natural comparisons and canonical common-field normalization. No full-faithfulness, essential-image or smallness clause is concluded.

source.place: Native realization proof steps 2--5, with the geometric hypotheses provided explicitly.

proof.text: Put $A_T^c=p_T^*\underline\Omega$ for the finite-subextension-valued condensed coefficient of the existing finite-subfield coefficient cocone. The coefficient assertion in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-function-coefficients] supplies a canonical isomorphism $A_T^c\cong(F_\ell)^\#_T$, where $F_\ell(V)$ consists of continuous functions $|V|\to\Omega$ taking values in one finite extension. Its sheafification is exactly $B_T$. Indeed, a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-subspace of $\Omega$ is contained in the finite field generated by a finite basis; conversely a finite extension is finite dimensional. Hence a locally finite function has a Zariski open cover on whose members it belongs to $F_\ell$. Such opens are pro-etale covers. The inclusion $F_\ell\to B$ is injective on every section set. Any two local representatives mapping to the same function agree on overlaps, and every section of $B$ has the displayed local lifts; sheaf gluing therefore makes $(F_\ell)^\#\to B$ an isomorphism. It preserves pointwise ring operations and restriction. This identifies $A_T^c$ canonically with $B_T$, including the inclusions from every finite field. For finite $E$, [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations] identifies $E_T^c$ with continuous $E$-valued functions and respects coefficient inclusions; [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] identifies that same sheaf with $B_{T,E}[1/\varpi_E]$. These are the coefficient maps in the displayed formula for $J_T$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12; Lemma 6.8.2; native locally-finite specialization, with the finite-span argument written here

proof.text: Identify native internal modules with modules in abelian sheaves by restriction to the constant scalar action and the inverse balanced action. Apply the section-module equivalence and normalized coefficient-ring scalar transport. The additive exact equivalences induce shift-compatible triangulated derived functors. No assertion of constructibility or descent is required in this step.

For a finite $E$, apply [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] on $T$. It gives the equivalence $R_{T,E}:D^b_c(T,E)\simeq\mathcal C_T^c(E)$, with $R_{T,E}(K_E)=E_T\otimes^L_{B_{T,E}}K_E$ and $R_{T,E}(u/\varpi_E^n)=\varpi_E^{-n}R_{T,E}(u)$. This is a statement about all ambient derived Hom groups, including shifted targets. Its completed integral source is the one defining $D^b_c(T,E)$ above: [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] explicitly identifies the compatible-etale-origin category with [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] on the schemes of step 1. Both rationalizations are raw, with the same objects and localized Hom groups; no idempotent completion is inserted. Their scalar-extension functors are not literally equal: the finite stages of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] use the strict-tower completed extension of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], while the realization statements use $T_{L/E}$ of the completed integral categories. [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] gives the identity equivalences $J_{T,E}$ together with the natural isomorphisms $j_{T,L/E}$, rationalizations of the inverse completion maps, which respect identities, shifts and the scalar associators on both sides; these are used in step 5. At field coefficients $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], so the finite stages are exactly the specified finite stages.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3); Proposition 6.8.14(2); integral presentation via Proposition 6.6.11

proof.text: The equivalences $R_{T,E}$ commute coherently with scalar extension. Precisely, after the comparison $j_{T,F/E}$ of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] from the scalar extension $K_E\otimes_EF$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] to the completed-category extension, [lem-per-rational-realization-scalar-coherence] identifies $R_{T,F}(K_E\otimes_EF)$ with $F_T\otimes^L_{E_T}R_{T,E}(K_E)$; since both families of comparisons respect the identity and three-field associator equations, so does the composite, including arbitrary ramification, raw fractions, identity and successive-field associators. The further extensions to $B_T=A_T^c$ have coherent tensor transitivity and are triangulated by [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus]. Apply the derived pullback composition comparison of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to the identity underlying topos with structural ring maps $B_{T,E}\to E_T\to B_T$. Thus the composite on a finite integral representative is the specified $B_T\otimes^L_{B_{T,E}}K_E$: flatten $b\otimes(e\otimes k)$ to $be\otimes k$, and insert $1$ for the inverse. The same balancing identifies its fractional morphisms with multiplication by the same inverse uniformizer power. These comparisons, and the equality after enlarging a common field, make $J_T$ well-defined on the pair category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Identity, composition and the independence of representatives follow by doing each finite diagram over one common field; the coherence just cited makes the two flattened composites equal.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14, common finite-field passage; balanced scalar normalizations as in the cited realization-scalar-coherence statement
